# tlinalg

> Tensor-free linear algebra kernels in Rust over faer, batched at every entry point, with borrowed workspaces and caller owned parallelism.

`tlinalg` wraps the dense kernels a tensor code needs (factorizations, solves, and the small
helpers around them) without introducing a tensor type of its own. Every execution entry point is
batched: an input is column-major items in batch order (first batch axis fastest), and the lane
decision belongs to the caller through `tcontract_exec::BatchPolicy`. Scratch is supplied by the
caller and parallel work runs on a caller owned `threadteam` team. There is no global thread pool.

Work estimates are part of the API: `estimate_work::<T>(shape args) -> f64` and
`estimate_payback_work::<T>(shape args) -> f64` describe one batch item in weighted multiply-adds,
not in time. `svd::estimate`, `qr::estimate` and `eigh::estimate` return the same count next to an
advisory `Duration`: `None` unless the caller measured this host with
`estimate::Rates::calibrate()` (opt-in, one short probe), and never a scheduling input.

## Key documentation

- [README](README.md): scope, the batch API, and the parallel model.
- [API reference](https://docs.rs/tlinalg): public types, batch entry points, and error types.
- [Batched API](docs/design/batched-api.md): why the batch is the unit, and what a call owns.
- [t4a-faer usage skill](https://github.com/tensor4all/faer/blob/main/skills/faer-usage/SKILL.md): the
  dense matrix library this provider calls (package `t4a-faer`, imported as `faer`) — decomposition
  choice, scratch sizing, and the caller owned `Par`; read it when the unit is one matrix instead of
  a batch.
- [Borrowed workspaces](docs/design/borrowed-workspace.md): the scratch contract and its sizing.
- [Team payback](docs/design/team-payback.md): when a batch is worth attaching a team to.
- [Estimate rates](docs/design/estimate-rates.md): work counts, the calibrated rate table, and why a
duration is advisory.
- [Repository rules](AGENTS.md): conventions for changes, tests, and benchmarking.

## Repository

- GitHub: https://github.com/tensor4all/tlinalg-rs
- Language: Rust (edition 2021), workspace at the repository root.
